key_insight: Plasticity in layered GeSe is not intrinsic or universal; it depends strongly on orientation, sample size, and loading path, with sliding and fracture competing under different constraints.
engineering_relevance: Flexible electronics should not classify an inorganic semiconductor as plastic from a single test, because device reliability on curved or strained surfaces requires multi-mode, multi-scale mechanical validation.
method: Bending along the c-axis armchair direction
Micropillar compression: conventional vs. eccentric loading
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~23% compressive strain without fracture in macroscopic loading, brittle cleavage under bending, brittle fragmentation in conventional micropillars, and enhanced interlayer sliding under eccentric micropillar shear.
watch_item: A positive result in one direction or test may overstate plasticity, since defects, stress constraints, and loading geometry can suppress or trigger different failure modes.
paper_title: Identifying Plastic Inorganic Semiconductors Requires More Rigorous Criteria
